newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller in opposition for first time.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller in opposition for first time.

text.p: Tansu Ciller on Monday handed over her post as Turkey's foreign minister to a left-wing MP in a government shake-up and moved into opposition for the first time since she entered parliament six years ago.
Ciller earlier gave way to leftist leader Bulent Ecevit as deputy prime minister. She had held both posts in the previous Islamist-led government.
"Congratulations," a Ciller told new Foreign Minister Ismail Cem in a brief speech at the foreign ministry.
Cem, a member of Ecevit's Democratic Left Party, arrived at the ministry carrying a bouquet of red roses for a short ceremony.
President Suleyman Demirel had earlier appointed Mesut Yilmaz as the new prime minister, triggering a wave of office clearances across the capital.

Ciller, a U.S.-trained economist, became a state minister in her maiden year as an MP in 1991. She was voted as Moslem but secular Turkey's first woman prime minister at a congress of her True Path Party in 1993 and has held various posts since then.
She has been criticised by the secularist establishment for going into coalition last year with the Islam-based Welfare Party of Necmettin Erbakan, who had produced corruption charges against her.
Erbakan resigned on June 18 after months of pressure from the secularist army.
Ciller now faces the dual challenges of opposition and a full-scale party rebellion. Around a fifth of the True Path's deputies have quit since she joined the Islamists in power.
The latest wave of resignations has given Yilmaz's anti-Islamist coalition a strong chance of winning a vote of confidence.
